approach.method_basis: The Parent generates fresh molecular graphs through a source-conditioned fragment editor alongside graph crossover. A small graph neural network chooses an attachment site and corpus-derived fragment, or a directed bond deletion. Its exact-action cache removes already known failures and currently duplicate products from proposal mass. An accepted-score count-fingerprint Gaussian process selects which generated molecules are purchased, with a posterior-mean screen after stalled batches; real scores update the archive and score-ranked breeding population. The editor currently learns by unweighted likelihood only from purchased edits that beat the real incumbent frozen before their batch was announced. It keeps those few records permanently within the session and makes 25 updates after feedback.
approach.novelty: Replace that binary success gate with all-outcome advantage-weighted exact-action likelihood. Every purchased policy action remains in replay, with a fixed positive exponential weight determined by its real score relative to the incumbent and score scale known before announcement. This preserves graded evidence from unsuccessful and tied actions while giving larger incumbent-relative gains more influence. There are no same-Parent siblings. Earlier editor children changed admissible proposal support and then hard replay eligibility; this child changes the learning objective using all observed actions. Whether that extra information produces more ordinary-route incumbent progress is the new test; more replay rows or higher fitted likelihood alone will not establish it.

observed_bottleneck: Actual code Parent n-db9d21d15567 discards most accepted exact policy actions at its strict incumbent-success replay gate. Its complete Search panel contains 1907 ordinary purchases, all represented policy actions, but only 127 replay records (54 additions, 73 deletions), 1..25 per session and three sessions without an addition replay positive. It nevertheless performs 10175 finite gradient updates and changes 1318 later paid raw-action probabilities, so its refuted useful-transfer prediction is not a recovery case or an inactive-learner diagnosis. Equal-session full ordinary-route sequential incumbent-gain mass is 0.09225374893829727 versus its own code Parent n-a8f828a5ff9b at 0.11494158661540828. Its endpoint mean is 0.5460054307238137 (seed SD 0.018127423721745226), with actual-Parent mean difference -0.001173508118584336; the separate formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de remains 0.607030316211131. The direct read-only audit in policy/scratch/r0078-02-improve-L01/plan/support-audit.json, with fifteen audit-seed-N-task files citing the original logs and trajectories, reproduces all 4350 labels, 4200 next-fit joins, 150 terminal censors and the primary baseline exactly. Applying the already frozen weight arithmetic passively to those historical receipts yields 1773 negative, seven zero and 127 positive advantages, 81..161 available actions per session, and effective sample sizes 3.6319989836508757..145.10276955347527. Those are construction-opportunity measurements on the Parent trajectory, not Child outcomes or evidence that lost stepping stones caused the decline. The scoped admission-efficiency confirmation of n-a8f828a5ff9b and full source-gain confirmation of n-cd97f70a82cb remain intact; their endpoint losses and the smaller-gain counterexample n-030a6ccbba7c prevent equating exposure, local wins or denser credit with final optimization success.

adoptions.applicability: The actual Parent already executes exact-action likelihood and chronological accepted-feedback joins, but its hard incumbent gate retains only 127 of 1907 paid policy actions, 1..25 per session. This single objective variant uses the available less-successful labels with smaller positive imitation weights; it does not apply a negative likelihood penalty to negative advantages. The policy is still filtered by the inherited GP purchaser and admission cache, so AWR policy-improvement or off-policy correction guarantees are not imported. The fixed beta, clipping, one-step baseline adaptation and normalized minibatch loss remain frozen even if effective weights concentrate.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Exponential advantage-weighted likelihood of replayed observed actions, with a finite upper weight cap.

deviations.adopted_setting: One-step score-minus-prospective-incumbent divided by prospective inherited score scale, beta 1, log-weight clipping to [-50, log(20)], session-local complete paid-action replay.
deviations.paper_setting: Long-horizon RL with a fitted value function, beta 0.05 and large replay.
deviations.reason: The incumbent is observed and frozen; no learned critic or unobserved return is invented. Fixed normalized weights test a new objective, not a threshold retune.

adoptions.implementation_change: In optimize.py Evolution.suggest/observe, save the common current-real-archive incumbent and GP population-score scale before announcement and carry them unchanged with the exact action to feedback. In external/fragment_editor.py FragmentEditor.feedback, retain every uniquely reconciled accepted policy action with immutable y, b, s, A and w. In train_after_feedback replace only the unweighted mean negative raw-action log likelihood by -sum(w*log_q_raw)/sum(w) on the inherited uniform minibatch; retain the same network, optimizer and update count.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the exact frozen r78-window9-feedback-support-review and position 3 of policy/scratch/search_policy-146d13ebf75c/literature-adoptions.json; no new search is claimed and actual queries remain in the cited review. Adopt only exponential advantage-weighted observed-action likelihood with a finite upper weight cap, on the measured exact-action Parent. Freeze the one-step incumbent/score-scale adaptation, beta=1, log clipping [-50,log(20)] and sum-of-weights minibatch denominator. The Parent evidence justifies testing information discarded by its hard replay gate, not claiming causal lost stepping stones. Retain the review deviations: no value network, discounted return, long-horizon control or imported policy-improvement/importance-correction guarantee. The full weighted objective is new and unmeasured on this approach; existing MARS introduction, earlier two follow-ups, investment, refutations and component gaps remain. No external model, asset, dependency or preparation input is needed.

sources.applicability: Borrow weighted action likelihood on measured editor actions. Use a one-step observed incumbent reference and prospective score scale, not a fitted long-horizon critic; freeze the adaptation explicitly and test useful transfer.
sources.finding: Replay actions can train a policy through exponential advantage-weighted likelihood. The full algorithm also fits a value baseline; its experiments cap weights at twenty.
sources.title: Advantage-Weighted Regression: Simple and Scalable Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning

hypothesis: One modification of the existing learned-editor objective: immutable signed incumbent-relative exponential weighting of every real accepted ordinary policy action. For each announcement freeze b as the maximum score in the complete real accepted archive and s as its inherited float64 population-score standard deviation with the unchanged positive GP floor 0.001; every member uses the same b and s. For each uniquely reconciled exact policy source/action with accepted real score y, store it once and freeze A=(y-b)/s, beta=1, log_w=clip(A,-50,log(20)), w=exp(log_w). Retain negative, zero and positive advantages with strictly positive weights; never apply source-success or incumbent-success membership. Crossover and fallbacks without an exact editor action provide no invented policy record. For each inherited uniform without-replacement minibatch minimize L=-sum_i(w_i*log q_raw(a_i|source_i))/sum_i(w_i), with detached immutable float64 weights, a strictly positive denominator and no epsilon or subsequent weight recomputation. q_raw remains log(0.5) plus the original supported site/fragment or directed-cut log factors; admission log_Z is excluded from this loss. All outcomes therefore influence action imitation in graded amounts rather than only passing or failing a gate. The hypothesis is that this changes learned action probabilities used in later paid edits and increases the full zero-inclusive ordinary-route incumbent-gain mass on the retained host. Raw-likelihood increase, label count, sign coverage and effective sample size measure exposure and objective execution, not useful transfer.

finding_summary.headline: Weighted replay increases ordinary-route progress, but final mean score falls
finding_summary.insights: The experiment rules out missing all-outcome membership and inactive learning as explanations for the remaining endpoint gap. It also shows why route progress must stay separate from total optimization success: ordinary actions account for more of the realized gains while crossover accounts for fewer, and the two path-dependent sums share one evolving incumbent. The largest task-level route increase is in docking, where mean ordinary gain rises by 0.289513 but the endpoint rises by only 0.001208. This supports the registered route-progress result without establishing mediation, reliable generalization or an independent benefit of the editor over crossover. Dense storage does not ensure broad effective learning. Sessions retain 99 to 191 records, but effective sample size ranges from 4.43 to 176.25; two sitagliptin sessions have only about 4.5 effective records despite storing 150 and 103 actions. Negative outcomes remain positively imitated with lower weights rather than receiving a negative penalty, and their aggregate replay weight mass exceeds the positive-outcome mass. Full-replay weighted loss improves in 354 blocks and worsens in 81; one terminal addition is never sampled, seven later paid actions show no audited probability change, and most ordinary purchases still make no incumbent progress. These are retained exposure limits, not grounds to retune the frozen law or change its falsifier. The trajectories and molecular assessment point to local concentration and uneven access to useful connected structures. Typed/generic scaffold coverage falls from 1,456/1,151 to 1,042/802, and fragment-excluded within-session nearest-neighbor similarity rises from 0.7931 to 0.8000. The population still has many ring and amine families, so this is not complete scaffold collapse. The large-molecule tail expands, with repeated-core examples, while compact fragments, unusual attachment/charge states and unassigned stereochemistry persist. A proposal operator or search scheme capable of coherent core and linker changes could address this limitation; these data do not isolate the GP ranker as its cause or establish that diversification would improve scores. The borrowed advantage-weighted likelihood operated, but the one-step observed-incumbent adaptation has no fitted value network, discounted return or imported policy-improvement guarantee. This result settles the registered all-outcome weighted-replay progress prediction and rejects its endpoint-improvement target on this panel. It leaves broader editor designs, retained-component contributions and the mechanism linking changed action probabilities to final scores open; it does not revise the earlier sparse-replay refutation or decide whether the approach should end.
finding_summary.results: The registered progress prediction is confirmed on the complete paired panel. All 2,250 purchased editor actions entered replay, versus 127 of 1,907 in the code Parent. They comprise 2,077 negative, 26 tied and 147 positive incumbent-relative outcomes. The frozen references, immutable weights, exact raw-action loss and seeded minibatches passed the full audit. There were 10,875 finite gradient updates and 2,166 later purchased actions with changed raw probabilities, versus 10,175 and 1,318 in the Parent. Every session showed later paid learning exposure. All 4,350 accepted purchases and 4,200 nonterminal next-fit joins reconciled; 150 terminal labels remain observed with future use censored. Mean full-session ordinary-route incumbent gain rose from 0.092254 to 0.166822, a gain of 0.074568, so the registered downstream falsifier did not trigger. Eight of fifteen paired sessions improved and seven declined; seed-mean changes were +0.028707, +0.230762 and -0.035765. Late ordinary gain rose from 0.021042 to 0.066664, although five sessions had zero late ordinary progress. Full/late positive source-gain means rose from 0.004283/0.003398 to 0.006251/0.006729. These gains did not improve the endpoint: final mean score was 0.540391 versus 0.546005, a paired change of -0.005615, missing the separate +0.002 target. Seed macro changes were -0.030884, +0.012073 and +0.001966. Crossover incumbent gain fell from 0.245260 to 0.165076 as ordinary purchases increased from 1,907 to 2,250. The separate formal Anchor averaged 0.607030; the Child trails it by 0.066640. Trusted paired task safety passes against the code Parent and fails against that Anchor on sitagliptin. Eligibility is not decided here.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic carbonyls, aryl amines and fused diones; narrower scaffold coverage, enlarged size tails and unresolved stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: This is an assessment of accepted molecular output from n-d781e302f9f5, paired with actual code Parent n-db9d21d15567. The frozen comparison separately marks Child evaluation and Parent pairing complete for Search seeds 0, 1 and 2. All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent trajectory files were read; no task, input path or paired chemistry comparison is missing. Each side contains 4350 accepted optimizer records, with the fixed initial records retained in audits and excluded from population descriptors. These trajectories do not cover every internally generated, rejected or unpurchased graph. The formal Anchor is a different comparator and is not substituted for the code Parent. The dominant products are indole/azaindole carbonyl compounds, thioamides and N-rich aromatic assemblies, halogenated aryl amines, sulfonyl-bearing cyclic amines and fused diones. Digest ring-closure text-presence rates span 0.9506 to 0.9816 and aromatic text-presence rates 0.9425 to 0.9759; these are molecule-level presence rates, not ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. RDKit parses all 4350 accepted Child molecules. Median size is 30 heavy atoms, median perceived ring count 4 and median aromatic ring count 3; size spans 1 to 119 heavy atoms. Parent median size is 29, with the same ring medians and range 1 to 120. Chemistry is uneven: Child N-halogen, O-halogen, divalent O-O and acyl-halide flags occur in 371, 156, 94 and 17 records, versus Parent 284, 120, 96 and 56 under identical definitions. The small all-aromatic-atom ring flag falls from 113 to 3. These overlapping structural flags require chemical scrutiny; none measures stability, toxicity or synthetic accessibility. Tiny products of at most 6 heavy atoms decrease from 179 to 154, while products of at least 50 increase from 275 to 432. Formal charges occur in 339 Child records versus 18 Parent records: the Child charged families include N-O anions and multiply charged quaternary-nitrogen assemblies, not demonstrated physiologic protonation sampling. No Child or Parent proposal has an assigned atom stereocentre; 1861 Child records contain unassigned centres versus 1572 Parent records. Global typed/generic Murcko coverage contracts to 1042/802 scaffolds from Parent 1456/1151, counting the empty scaffold as one. This is moderate diversity with local convergence, not complete scaffold collapse. The inherited fragment-excluded nearest-neighbor diagnostic retains 4196 Child and 4171 Parent records; its pooled median is 0.8 versus 0.7931034482758621. Each nearest neighbor is sought only within its own seed/task/side, using radius-2 chirality-aware 2048-bit Morgan Tanimoto after excluding molecules of at most 6 heavy atoms. Counts and similarity show related products rather than independent scaffold families; higher similarity is not itself an efficacy result. The high and low strata below each comprise the highest or lowest 29 optimizer scores per seed, pooled to 87 per task; ties use ascending score/evaluation order, with the high slice taking the final 29. Molecular metrics retain the code Parent definitions. Ring perception can count symmetry-related cycles. The aliphatic-carbon amide/carbonyl SMARTS do not count every aromatic lactam or dione, so functional-group prose also reads the SMILES. The broad nonamide saturated-ring-nitrogen flag is not a basicity measurement; the supplemental carbon-bound neutral-amine flag excludes N bonded to heteroatoms and carbon centers doubly bonded to N/O/S. No unobserved target pharmacophore, stereoisomer preference, binding pose, synthesis route or universal chemical cutoff is inferred. Scores are the supplied observations; shared initials, seeds and ancestry make these descriptive chemistry associations. They do not judge the weighted-likelihood mechanism, useful transfer or retained-component contribution. No runtime or peak-memory inference is made. Frozen request: policy/requests/r0078-02-improve-L01-molecular-assess-bd7d5f069920cc6a.json. Descriptor audit: policy/scratch/r0078-02-improve-L01/molecular/summary.json. Similarity/amine/charge audit: policy/scratch/r0078-02-improve-L01/molecular/similarity.json. Original-to-copy mappings and raw hashes: policy/scratch/r0078-02-improve-L01/molecular/provenance.json. The per-task entries cite every paired raw trajectory and derived audit; the manifest also preserves byte-identical Child run logs and summaries and the published Parent run logs and summaries.

Median size is 25 heavy atoms with 3 perceived and aromatic rings, range 1 to 35 heavy atoms; Parent median size is 24 with the same ring median. The seed-0 leader is a 24-heavy-atom azaindole bearing a dicarbonyl-imine-phenyl chain. Seed 1 favors a 24-heavy-atom N-formyl indole anilide with methyl and fluoromethyl substituents. The indole-amide building blocks are recognizable synthetic chemistry; the anionic N-O, alpha-halogenated amine/aldehyde and adjacent carbonyl/imine motifs raise additional stability and preparation questions. method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
